526.t: The Jazz Composers Orchestra at Newport
526.s: After the Guild broke up, she and Michael Mantler kept the orchestra and played Newport where audiences hated it and Billy Taylor refused to announce it.
526.q: And so me and Michael Mantler used everybody in the whole guild in the orchestra. And, it was just something that you did, you played in the orchestra if you were in the guild. But, uhh, when the guild fell through, six months later.... arguing all the time, people just screamed. And uhh, me and…

526.t: The Anti-Festival and how the band got booked at Newport
526.s: She recalls the Newport anti-festival, an afternoon slot, and guesses the Guild's press got them booked, with Kimery noting Wein's broad programming.
526.q: Well I don’t know. I had played earlier at the Anti-Festival, you know there was maybe... there was another festival at Hilton at the same time and people who played like that kind of music were in it. It was in Newport in a tent, same town, same time, and we were having a festival to complain…

627.t: Fiddlers and guitarists heard at Newport
627.s: Cage says few fiddlers were at Newport, one from Connecticut, and a good white guitarist.
627.ch: Cage on musicians, travels and old songs
627.q: North of the city, I went to Newport. They had plenty of them up there. Mm-mm. They had one from Canada. Canada, Connecticut, whatever they call that place. Connecticut. Yes. You know his name? No, sir. I don't know his name.

588.t: The Newport protest and sick, crazy musicians
588.s: She recalls Roach, Mingus and Max Gordon's festival protest and the East 74th Street Theater.
588.ch: Venues, circuits and the music business
588.q: Well, George is only human. He's got a certain group of people he likes. He doesn't like everybody. They didn't care that much for George either, but they wanted him to give them a job. Anyway, we have it on tape. We were all a bunch of bandits then, Roach and Charles Mingus and -­

62.t: City suites and the Monterey Jazz Festival
62.s: Brown compares Wilson's city compositions to Duke's suites; Wilson recounts Jimmy Lyons, the Jubilee broadcasts and his 1963 Monterey invitation.
62.ch: Recent recordings, Monterey and signature works
62.q: Oh that was a thrill, you know. I didn’t – you know the Monterey Jazz Festival started in 1958, right? Well I didn’t get to go there until five years – but I knew the guy who started it.

576.t: Performing with George Russell at Newport and later
576.s: She appeared with Russell's sextet at Newport in 1964, at the Modern Museum of Art and later in Boston, usually only to sing Sunshine.
576.ch: Europe and a single mother's career
576.q: Well, that, those were the only two I did. I mean, I did the Newport and then I did one at the museum, I think… Modern Museum of Art one time. I don‟t remember what that was for, but those are the only times that I, that I appeared with George, and it was only, it was only to do Sunshine. And then,…

614.t: Festival appearances, a Boston Common one-shot, and closing the 1950s
614.s: He recalls other festivals and a Boston Common concert tape, says anyone who survived the 1950s should be congratulated, and mentions Jazzland recordings.
614.q: I heard a tape not too long ago that was sent to me by a friend, Joe McDonald in San Francisco, a drummer. He worked with me for a short period of time, and was a good friend of Bill Paul Harris'. And they arranged -- the Arts

117.t: Newport Jazz Festival years and the Steve Allen Show
117.s: Freeman says he played fourteen Newport festivals, and George Wein hired him back after seeing him on the live Steve Allen Show.
117.q: Allen. Now, George Wein, a very interesting thing, had not hired me that year for the Newport Jazz Festival. I did 14 Newport Jazz Festivals, 14 years. I was in four riots in those years, and now he had not hired me for the Newport Festival this particular year, but I did the Steve Allen Show and…

388.t: Newport Festivals and the New Jersey Jazz Society
388.s: Leeman plays the first Newport Festival with Condon, who conducted under an umbrella in the rain, and later New York Newport and Waterloo Village concerts.
388.q: I must mention -- I did the first year of the Newport Festivals were starting, with Eddie Condon, for George Wein, Schroeder he was the promoter. We had Peanuts Hucko, Jack Lesberg, Gene Shrader, and Cutty Cutshall among others. And it rained

170.t: Back to New York in 1960 and the rebel Newport festival
170.s: Ware pawns the fiddle, rides back with Walter Perkins, then plays the Jazz Artists counter-festival at Newport; the group folds.
170.ch: Back to Chicago and the road to jail and illness
170.q: It don't make sense. Then, on top of that, you got to keep up your other dues at your home local. But that's the way it went down. Anyway, they got me fined, and Johnny Griffin had a week at the Regal, a big band, you know, he wanted me to come in with him. But they wouldn't let me play. So I'm…

19.t: Dakota Staton at the 1960 Newport and Atlantic City festivals
19.s: Newport draws a rowdy non-jazz crowd, and in Atlantic City he hangs out with Oscar Peterson.
19.ch: Al Hibbler, Dakota Staton and later years
19.q: 1960... We left there and went to Atlantic City, and we played the Atlantic City Jazz Festival, which was quite an experience. I got to hang out with Oscar Peterson and the trio, and a lot of other people. We worked Atlantic City, and leaving there... I think we did a club there after the Festival.…

103.s: Jones recalls being house drummer at the first Newport festival in the rain, backing Billie Holiday with Hinton and Teddy Wilson.
103.q: Well, I had my drums there and it was raining. It started raining at 8 o'clock. Gene Krupa had to play on my drums. We played at the casino.....

239.t: Pat Suzuki's Newport Festival group and other Newport appearances
239.s: Jones led a seven-piece band at Newport with Pat Suzuki, Doc Severinsen, and played there with Anita O'Day and Sarah.
239.q: try to turn my mind off of out here and go way back to New York. Let's see, Pat Suzuki. Well, this was Doc Severinsen again, was in the band. I was the leader. Yes, I know what it was for. It was for the Newport Jazz Festival. We had about seven pieces, you know, and I had to do some writing for…
